metadata.description: Enriched dataset combining your DRI brackets with FDA Daily Values (DV) for a 2,000 kcal reference diet plus conversion rules and examples to compute %DV. Use fdaDailyValues to convert any measured nutrient amount -> percent Daily Value for label-style reporting.
metadata.lastUpdatedFromSources: FDA Daily Value reference guide (Aug 2023), FDA Nutrition Facts guidance, NIH ODS Daily Value summary

sources.name: FDA - Which nutrients must be listed on the label
FDA - Lows and Highs of %DV guidance
FDA - What's on the Nutrition Facts Label (guide)

notes: DV values are the single reference numbers used for %DV on the Nutrition Facts label (2,000 kcal reference).
%DV formula is: (amount_in_serving / DV_amount) * 100. See conversion.unitHandling for microgram/milligram handling.
Some nutrients (vitamin D, calcium, iron, potassium) must show both amount and %DV on the label; others may be voluntary.
Guidance: <=5% DV per serving is considered low; >=20% DV per serving is considered high.

added_sugars.note: FDA 2,000 kcal reference added sugars DV

cholesterol.note: historical labeling DV (declared amount required if present)

vitamin_D.note: DV set to 20 µg (800 IU) per FDA guidance

unitHandling.micrograms: if input is in 'µg' (micrograms) ensure DV is in µg; if input is in 'mg' convert to µg by multiplying mg*1000 or vice versa, matching the DV unit.
unitHandling.example: If user supplies 5 µg vitamin D and DV is 20 µg -> percentDV = (5/20)*100 = 25%
unitHandling.recommendedNormalization: Prefer normalizing numeric inputs to the DV unit before division. Provide explicit unit in API payload to avoid ambiguity.

roundingRecommendations.percentDV_display: Round to nearest whole percent for label-like displays; optionally show one decimal in UI.
roundingRecommendations.smallAmounts: Follow your UI/consumer rules; FDA label rules specify rounding conventions for amounts on labels (not directly for %DV): follow regulatory guidance if producing regulatory labels.

low_threshold.meaning: 5% DV or less per serving is considered low

high_threshold.meaning: 20% DV or more per serving is considered high

notes: Not every nutrient on the DRI dataset has an FDA DV (FDA may allow voluntary declaration). Use fdaDailyValues keys as authoritative for %DV computation.
Added Sugars has a DV of 50 g (2016 label update).

preferedUnits.mass: mg for minerals and mg/µg as appropriate; check fdaDailyValues.unit
preferedUnits.vitamins: match unit in fdaDailyValues (µg or mg as shown)
